Arke 

 A file explorer for Windows that never freezes. 
GPU-rendered, written in Rust, one small exe. 

 
 
 
 
 
 

 English · 简体中文 · 繁體中文 · 日本語 · Deutsch · Español · Português (Brasil) 

 

 Why Arke

 It stays responsive. Listing, sorting, thumbnails, folder sizes, search and file operations
all run off the UI thread. An unreachable network share or a folder with 100,000 files doesn't
stop you from scrolling, typing or switching tabs.

 It finds anything, instantly. Arke keeps a file name index of your local drives. With the
optional background service it reads the NTFS master file table directly, indexing millions of
files in seconds, and follows the change journal so the index is current the moment you open it.

 File operations don't keep you waiting. A folder of 20,000 files goes to the Recycle Bin in
0.2 s instead of 47 s in File Explorer, and restores as usual. Copies and moves show their progress,
queue up on the same drive, can be paused, and can be undone.

 It's built for working in many folders at once. Tabs live in a vertical sidebar, can be
pinned and saved as named workspaces. Any tab splits into two panes that browse in sync or compare
their contents, and dragging a file onto a tab, a favorite or a path segment drops it right
there.

 It's safe with your system. Arke has no telemetry. Apart from the optional search service, which
Windows registers when you install it, Arke writes to the registry only if you turn on
"Open folders in Arke": then it registers itself as the folder handler for your Windows account
(under HKEY CURRENT USER\Software\Classes only), and turning the setting off puts everything back.
Shell extensions from other programs run in a separate process, so a buggy one can't take Arke down.

If Arke is useful to you, a ⭐ on GitHub helps other people find it.

Arke was featured in Ruan Yifeng's tech weekly 420 and is listed in awesome-rust, awesome-gpui and on AlternativeTo.

 

 Features

 
 
 
 
 
 
 Split any tab into two panes that browse in sync or compare their contents. 
 A fast context menu of its own, with the full Windows menu one click away. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Quick Look (Space) shows Markdown the way GitHub does, and images, PDF, Office files and code. 
 A Properties window of its own (Alt+Enter) that shows where a folder's space goes. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Details, icons and columns views, with a preview pane for most kinds of files. 
 Light, dark and dark gray themes, accent colors, and a background tint or image. 
 
 

 Browse 
- Details, icons (any size up to 256 px, Ctrl+mouse wheel) and columns views. In Details, folders
 can expand in place, and you can sort by several columns, reorder columns and show link targets.
- Each folder remembers its view and sort.
- Tabs you can pin or save as workspaces. Split a tab into two panes with one shared preview,
 synchronized browsing and folder compare. Middle-click or Ctrl+click a folder in the sidebar, on
 Home or in the address bar to open it in a new tab (Ctrl+double-click in the file list).
- The search box sits in the middle of the title bar and searches the active pane. Each pane has
 its own row with Up, its path and its view buttons, so in split view each side keeps its own
 filter.
- Drag a tab out to give it a window of its own, or drop files on a tab to copy or move them into
 its folder.
- Favorites at the top of the sidebar and on Home, as tiles and a list: add a folder or a tab from
 its menu, or drag it there. Drag them to reorder (the others make room, like app icons on a
 phone) or out to remove them, and rename them without renaming the folder. Folders pinned to
 Quick Access in File Explorer show up too.
- One window by default (since 0.7): folders from other apps, Win+E and starting Arke again add a
 tab to the window you used last. Turn off "Single window" in settings for a window each.
- With "New windows open to: Last tabs", the windows open when you quit Arke (or Windows shuts
 down) come back with their tabs. A window you close while others stay open isn't kept.
- Spring-loaded folders, a shelf for collecting files from different folders, and a Home page
 with your favorites, recent files, drives and network locations, each with its own right-click
 menu (drives get eject, Format, Disk Cleanup and Properties).
- Swipe with two fingers on a touchpad to go back and forward, like in a browser.
- The sidebar can be made wider by dragging its edge and collapses to a column of icons (Ctrl+B),
 which can be set to open over the content when you rest the pointer on it (off by default).
 Favorites, This PC and Network each collapse with a click on their heading, and the folder tree
 follows the folder you're in. Columns in the columns view can be resized.
- Interface scale from 80% to 150%, on top of Windows' own scale.
- Command palette (Ctrl+Shift+P) for every command, and shortcuts you can change.

 Preview 
- A resizable preview pane and Quick Look (Space) for images (SVG too), PDF, Word, Excel and
 PowerPoint, text and code with syntax highlighting, Markdown, archives, .gz files and folders.
- Videos show a frame and PDFs their first page as their thumbnail. Quick Look zooms text, documents and PDF pages
 (Ctrl+wheel), and with QuickLook installed, Space can open that instead.

- As you type, in this folder, its subfolders or the whole computer, with fuzzy matching and

- Search inside files, including PDF and Office documents, in a folder and its subfolders.

install.title: Install
install.html:
Download from Releases. Both downloads are the same Arke, with the same features and updates, and both keep settings in %APPDATA%\Arke:

  • Portable, arke-<version>.exe: a single exe with no runtime that runs from any folder. Nothing is installed, so it isn't in the Start menu or in Settings › Apps; Settings › About › Remove Arke from this PC removes it.
  • Installer, arke-<version>-setup.exe: installs Arke for your account without administrator approval, or for all users in Program Files, and adds it to the Start menu and to Settings › Apps, where you can uninstall it.

On ARM64 PCs, use the -arm64 files (arke-<version>-arm64.exe, arke-<version>-arm64-setup.exe).

With Scoop:

scoop bucket add arke https://github.com/Koimsurai/scoop-bucket
scoop install arke/arke

Scoop then keeps it up to date (scoop update arke), and Arke leaves updating to it.

Builds aren't code-signed yet, so SmartScreen may ask for confirmation the first time. Signing through SignPath Foundation is on the way, see Code signing policy.

Arke checks GitHub for a new version at most once a day and only installs one when you say so (Settings › About). Updates are signed: Arke installs only files signed with its own key. Where GitHub is slow, you can set a download route there (see Privacy).

Optional background service

Settings › Search › Live updates installs a small Windows service, with administrator approval. It reads only the file system's change journal and master file table, never file contents, and never reports names inside other users' profile folders. You can remove it from the same place.

features.title: Features
features.html:
Split any tab into two panes that browse in sync or compare their contents. A fast context menu of its own, with the full Windows menu one click away.

Details, icons and columns views, with a preview pane for most kinds of files. Light, dark and dark gray themes, accent colors, and a background tint or image.

Browse

  • Details, icons (any size up to 256 px, Ctrl+mouse wheel) and columns views. In Details, folders can expand in place, and you can sort by several columns, reorder columns and show link targets.
  • Each folder remembers its view and sort.
  • Tabs you can pin or save as workspaces. Split a tab into two panes with one shared preview, synchronized browsing and folder compare. Middle-click or Ctrl+click a folder in the sidebar, on Home or in the address bar to open it in a new tab (Ctrl+double-click in the file list).

  • Drag a tab out to give it a window of its own, or drop files on a tab to copy or move them into its folder.
  • Favorites at the top of the sidebar and on Home, as tiles and a list: add a folder or a tab from its menu, or drag it there. Drag them to reorder (the others make room, like app icons on a phone) or out to remove them, and rename them without renaming the folder. Folders pinned to Quick Access in File Explorer show up too.
  • One window by default (since 0.7): folders from other apps, Win+E and starting Arke again add a tab to the window you used last. Turn off "Single window" in settings for a window each.
  • With "New windows open to: Last tabs", the windows open when you quit Arke (or Windows shuts down) come back with their tabs. A window you close while others stay open isn't kept.
  • Spring-loaded folders, a shelf for collecting files from different folders, and a Home page with your favorites, recent files, drives and network locations, each with its own right-click menu (drives get eject, Format, Disk Cleanup and Properties).
  • Swipe with two fingers on a touchpad to go back and forward, like in a browser.
  • The sidebar can be made wider by dragging its edge and collapses to a column of icons (Ctrl+B), which can be set to open over the content when you rest the pointer on it (off by default). Favorites, This PC and Network each collapse with a click on their heading, and the folder tree follows the folder you're in. Columns in the columns view can be resized.
  • Interface scale from 80% to 150%, on top of Windows' own scale.
  • Command palette (Ctrl+Shift+P) for every command, and shortcuts you can change.

Preview

  • A resizable preview pane and Quick Look (Space) for images (SVG too), PDF, Word, Excel and PowerPoint, text and code with syntax highlighting, Markdown, archives, .gz files and folders.
  • Videos show a frame and PDFs their first page as their thumbnail. Quick Look zooms text, documents and PDF pages (Ctrl+wheel), and with QuickLook installed, Space can open that instead.

Search

  • As you type, in this folder, its subfolders or the whole computer, with fuzzy matching and filters for type, size and date (search syntax).
  • Search inside files, including PDF and Office documents, in a folder and its subfolders.
  • Files and folders you open often come first in whole-computer results.

Files

  • Copy and move through the Windows shell engine with progress, undo and redo. Jobs on the same drive queue up and can be paused, with optional verify after copy or hand-off to TeraCopy (experimental).
  • Batch rename, "Move to new folder", and a move/copy/shortcut menu when you drag with the right mouse button or drop with Alt held.
  • A Properties window of its own (Alt+Enter): sizes, where a folder's space goes, attributes, the app a file opens with, SHA-256 and unblocking downloaded files. Windows' own is one click away. A whole drive is counted in seconds, from the search index or, with the search service, from the drive's file table the way WizTree does.

Places

  • Network shares that fail fast when a server is offline and show the last known contents; \\server lists its shares. SFTP and WebDAV locations (experimental; plain http only after you allow it for that location). Mapped drives and network places can get names of their own, kept in Arke only.
  • OneDrive and other cloud folders with sync status. Previews never download online-only files.
  • Archives: preview and extract zip and 7z (password-protected ones too), tar (.gz, .xz, .bz2, .zst) and RAR, compress to zip. RAR and the xz / bzip2 / zstd tars use the libarchive built into Windows (best on Windows 11 23H2 and later).

Windows

  • Big folders go to the Recycle Bin at once on local drives: 20,000 files in about a quarter of a second instead of 40 s, since Windows doesn't check every file first. Restore works as usual, and anything it can't vouch for (network drives, OneDrive, files in use, policies) is left to Windows. It can be turned off in settings. Loose files take a few milliseconds each, still two to six times faster than Windows.
  • Updates download quietly in the background and install the next time Arke restarts, never while files are being copied and never over a metered connection.
  • Menus open in windows of their own, like Windows menus, so near the edge they reach past Arke's window instead of being squeezed. Windows commands you pin from "More options" (Git Bash, Windows Terminal, VS Code, 7-Zip, NanaZip...) show as soon as the menu opens, and Shift+right-click adds the extended ones, as in File Explorer.
  • Launchers and scripts (Listary, ALTRun, AutoHotkey, PowerShell) can read Arke's windows, tabs and selection and open folders through one JSON interface (docs/integration.md).
  • Quiet when idle: nothing on screen changing means nothing redrawn, minimized included. Folder sizes, indexing and the search service run at low priority in Windows' efficiency mode, and with only the tray icon left Arke frees its caches.
  • Optionally (experimental) open folders in Arke instead of File Explorer (folders opened from other apps included), also "Show in folder" from browsers and "Open file location" from other apps. It registers Arke as the folder handler for your account and is undone when you turn it off. File Explorer you start yourself (Win+E, the taskbar, Start) stays File Explorer unless you also turn on "Win+E and the File Explorer icon open Arke too".
  • Screen reader support, x64 and ARM64 builds (both tested on real hardware), taskbar jump list, safe USB eject, system tray, settings backup. English, Simplified and Traditional Chinese, Japanese, German, Spanish and Brazilian Portuguese (the last four are new in 0.8; corrections to the wording are welcome in issues).

Experimental features are covered by automated tests and local test servers but not yet widely used; see the changelog. Feedback in issues is welcome.
